title: The Four Virtues
aka: good sense, justice, courage and self-restraint
lead: Good sense (prudence), justice, courage and self-restraint (temperance): the four main virtues of Greek philosophy, named in Plato's Republic, taken up by Jewish writers in Greek (Wisdom of Solomon 8:7; 4 Maccabees 1:18) and called the "cardinal" virtues by the church.

sections.b: Plato's Socrates says of the good city: "Clearly, then, it will be wise, brave, sober, and just" (Republic 4.427e). The Wisdom of Solomon says that Wisdom "teaches self-control and understanding, / righteousness and courage" (Wisdom of Solomon 8:7). 4 Maccabees makes the four "kinds of wisdom", the training of the law (4 Maccabees 1:17-18). The Catholic Catechism calls them "cardinal" because "all the others are grouped around them", quotes the Wisdom of Solomon for them, and teaches that human virtues "are purified and elevated by divine grace" (Catechism 1805, 1810).
